_metadata.title: ComplianceLint Interim Standard for EU AI Act Article 4: AI Literacy
_metadata.disclaimer: This is an interim checklist developed by ComplianceLint. It is not a harmonised standard and does not itself give a presumption of conformity. No harmonised standard is requested for Article 4. The Regulation instead requires the Commission to publish practical examples of how to comply on the single information platform (Article 4(2)) and the Board to adopt recommendations setting out common objectives (Article 4(3)). The Commission has published an AI-literacy Q&A and a living repository of AI-literacy practices.
basis: EU AI Act Recital 20 (AI literacy) and Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Recital 8 (amendment of Article 4)
ISO/IEC 42001:2023 -- AI management system (Clause 7.2 Competence, 7.3 Awareness)
ISO/IEC TR 24368:2022 -- Overview of ethical and societal concerns
OECD AI Principles -- Human-centred values and fairness
UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021)
_metadata.awaiting_standard: No harmonised standard is requested for Article 4. The Regulation instead requires the Commission to publish practical examples of how to comply on the single information platform (Article 4(2)) and the Board to adopt recommendations setting out common objectives (Article 4(3)). The Commission has published an AI-literacy Q&A and a living repository of AI-literacy practices.

requirements.title: AI Literacy Measures
requirements.requirement: The provider or deployer of an AI system MUST take measures to support the development of AI literacy of its staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on its behalf (Article 4(1)); a structured AI literacy programme is the recommended way to do so. Article 4 prescribes no specific content or format; the content and formats listed below are recommended.
requirements.rationale: Art. 4(1), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, requires providers and deployers to 'take measures to support the development of AI literacy' of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf; it does not require them to guarantee any specific level of AI literacy of any individual.
required_content: Overview of AI capabilities and limitations relevant to the organization
Risks and potential biases of AI systems in use
Responsibilities when operating or relying on AI outputs
Affected persons and groups — how to consider their rights
Escalation procedures for uncertain or high-risk AI decisions
Regulatory context (EU AI Act basics relevant to role)
acceptable_formats: Workshop or seminar records with attendance
External certification programs (AI ethics, responsible AI)

requirements.title: AI Usage Policy
requirements.requirement: The organization SHOULD maintain an AI usage policy documenting how AI systems are to be operated and used by staff.
requirements.rationale: Art. 4(1) requires the AI literacy measures to take into account 'the context the AI systems are to be used in' and to consider 'the persons or groups of persons on whom the AI systems are to be used'. An AI usage policy is one way to document this; Art. 4 does not require a policy.
required_content: List of AI systems in use and their intended purposes
Approved use cases and explicitly prohibited uses
Data handling requirements when using AI systems
Incident reporting procedures for AI-related issues

requirements.title: Role-Specific Training Differentiation
requirements.requirement: The AI literacy measures MUST take into account the technical knowledge, experience, education and training of the persons concerned and the context the AI systems are to be used in, and consider the persons or groups of persons on whom the AI systems are to be used (Article 4(1)). Differentiating training by role SHOULD be used to achieve this.
requirements.rationale: Art. 4(1) requires the measures to take into account the technical knowledge, experience, education and training of the relevant persons. Any measures used must be designed so that those differences are taken into account.
acceptable_implementations: Developer track: AI/ML fundamentals, bias detection, testing
Operator track: system monitoring, escalation, override procedures
Decision-maker track: AI limitations, accountability, affected persons
Executive track: regulatory obligations, organizational responsibility

scoring.compliant: R01 met, with the measures taking into account the factors listed in R03 (R02 is recommended, not required)
scoring.partial: R01 partially met (some measures exist, but they do not take into account the factors listed in R03) or only R02 met
